### `shopping_mall_orders`

Main order records representing completed transactions in the e-commerce
platform.

Each order is created after successful payment and contains multiple
order items from potentially different sellers. The order status is
derived from the statuses of its constituent items according to business
rules: 'paid' when all items are paid, 'shipped' when any item is
shipped, 'delivered' when all items are delivered, 'cancelled' when all
items are cancelled, 'refunded' when all items are refunded, and
'partially_completed' for mixed statuses.

Orders are preserved indefinitely for legal compliance and audit
purposes. The shipping address is captured in an immutable snapshot (via
[shopping_mall_order_addresses](#shopping_mall_order_addresses)) at the time of order placement.
Each order item maintains its own status and references
product/variant/seller snapshots from the purchase time.

References:
- Customer: [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers)
- Address snapshot: [shopping_mall_order_addresses](#shopping_mall_order_addresses)
- Order items: [shopping_mall_order_items](#shopping_mall_order_items)

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_customer_id`
  > Customer who placed this order. References {@link
  > shopping_mall_customers.id}.
- `order_number`
  > Unique order identifier for customer reference and tracking.
  > Auto-generated in format like 'ORD-2024-001234'.
- `total_price`
  > Total price of the order calculated as the sum of all order item prices
  > (quantity × unit price). Stored as decimal for monetary precision.
- `status`
  > Derived order status computed from constituent order item statuses.
  > Values: 'paid' (all items paid), 'shipped' (any item shipped),
  > 'delivered' (all items delivered), 'cancelled' (all items cancelled),
  > 'refunded' (all items refunded), 'partially_completed' (mixed statuses).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the order was created after successful payment.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the order was last updated, such as when order item
  > statuses changed.

### `shopping_mall_order_addresses`

Immutable shipping address snapshots captured at order placement time for
legal compliance and audit trail purposes.

Each address record preserves the complete shipping information exactly
as it was when the customer placed the order, ensuring that historical
orders maintain accurate delivery records even if customers modify or
delete addresses from their address book.

Contains recipient name, phone number, street address, city,
state/province, postal code, and country. Records are append-only and
never modified after creation to maintain data integrity for dispute
resolution and legal compliance.

References [shopping_mall_orders](#shopping_mall_orders) via unique foreign key,
establishing a one-to-one relationship where each order has exactly one
shipping address snapshot.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_order_id`
  > Reference to the order this shipping address belongs to. Each order has
  > exactly one shipping address snapshot. [shopping_mall_orders.id](#shopping_mall_orders)
- `recipient_name`
  > Full name of the person designated to receive the shipment at the
  > delivery address.
- `phone`
  > Contact phone number for the recipient, used for delivery coordination
  > and shipping notifications.
- `street`: Street address including house/apartment number for the delivery location.
- `city`: City or locality name for the delivery address.
- `state`: State, province, or administrative region for the delivery address.
- `postal_code`: Postal or ZIP code for the delivery address.
- `country`: Country name or ISO country code for the delivery address.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this shipping address snapshot was created at order
  > placement. Immutable - no updated_at field as records are never modified.

### `shopping_mall_order_items`

Individual order items representing specific product variants purchased
by customers. Each item maintains independent status tracking (paid,
shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded) enabling item-level
cancellation/refund and multi-seller order handling. Contains complete
snapshot data for product, variant, and seller at time of purchase for
historical accuracy and dispute resolution. References the parent {@link
shopping_mall_orders} and the selling [shopping_mall_sellers](#shopping_mall_sellers).
Product and variant references may become null if source entities are
deleted, but snapshot data is preserved for order history integrity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_order_id`
  > The order this item belongs to. References {@link
  > shopping_mall_orders.id}.
- `shopping_mall_seller_id`
  > The seller who sold this item. References {@link
  > shopping_mall_sellers.id}.
- `shopping_mall_product_id`
  > The original product at time of purchase. May be null if product is
  > deleted. References [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products).
- `shopping_mall_product_variant_id`
  > The original variant at time of purchase. May be null if variant is
  > deleted. References [shopping_mall_product_variants.id](#shopping_mall_product_variants).
- `product_name`
  > Product name at time of purchase. Snapshot value preserved for historical
  > accuracy even if product is later edited or deleted.
- `product_description`
  > Product description at time of purchase. Snapshot value preserved for
  > historical accuracy.
- `product_category_name`
  > Product category name at time of purchase. Snapshot value for order
  > history display.
- `product_base_price`
  > Product base price at time of purchase. Snapshot value preserved for
  > price dispute resolution.
- `product_thumbnail_url`
  > Product main image URL at time of purchase. Snapshot value for order
  > history display.
- `variant_sku_code`
  > Variant SKU code at time of purchase. Unique identifier for the specific
  > product configuration.
- `variant_price`
  > Variant price at time of purchase (may override product base price).
  > Snapshot value preserved for historical accuracy.
- `seller_shop_name`
  > Seller shop name at time of purchase. Snapshot value preserved for order
  > history even if seller profile is later edited or account is deleted.
- `seller_shop_description`
  > Seller shop description at time of purchase. Snapshot value for
  > historical accuracy.
- `seller_logo_url`
  > Seller logo image URL at time of purchase. Snapshot value for order
  > history display.
- `quantity`
  > Number of units purchased for this variant. Multiple quantities of the
  > same variant are combined into a single order item.
- `unit_price`
  > Price per unit at time of purchase. Derived from variant price or product
  > base price. Total for this item = quantity * unit_price.
- `status`
  > Current status of this order item. Valid values: 'paid' (awaiting
  > shipment), 'shipped' (in transit), 'delivered' (received by customer),
  > 'cancelled' (cancelled before shipping), 'refunded' (refunded after
  > delivery). Each item has independent status enabling item-level
  > operations.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this order item was created. Set at order placement time
  > and immutable thereafter.

### `shopping_mall_order_shipments`

Shipment records created by sellers containing carrier information,
tracking details, and delivery confirmation data. Each shipment bundles
one or more order items from the same seller into a single package with
one tracking number. Created when seller ships items, triggering status
change to 'shipped' for all included order items. Delivery confirmation
can be manual (customer confirms) or automatic (14 days after shipment).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_seller_id`
  > Seller who created and shipped this package. {@link
  > shopping_mall_sellers.id}
- `carrier_name`: Name of the shipping carrier (e.g., 'FedEx', 'UPS', 'Korea Post').
- `tracking_number`: Tracking number provided by the carrier for shipment tracking.
- `shipped_at`: Timestamp when the shipment was created and items were shipped.
- `delivered_at`
  > Timestamp when delivery was confirmed (either by customer manually or
  > automatically after 14 days). Null until delivery is confirmed.
- `delivery_confirmation_method`
  > Method of delivery confirmation: 'manual' for customer-initiated, 'auto'
  > for automatic confirmation after 14 days. Null until delivery is
  > confirmed.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the shipment record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the shipment record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp for soft deletion. Null if shipment is active.

### `shopping_mall_order_item_variant_options`

Normalized key-value pairs capturing variant option values for order
items at the point of purchase.

Each record stores a single option attribute (e.g., key='color',
value='red') as an atomic unit, enabling proper 1NF compliance by
avoiding JSON or serialized string storage in the parent order item
table. This decomposition allows efficient querying by option type and
value, and preserves the exact variant configuration that the customer
purchased.

Created automatically when an order is placed, copying the option values
from the selected product variant. Part of the snapshot principle
implementation ensuring complete audit trails for dispute resolution.

References [shopping_mall_order_items.id](#shopping_mall_order_items) as the parent entity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_order_item_id`
  > The order item for which this variant option was captured. References
  > [shopping_mall_order_items.id](#shopping_mall_order_items).
- `key`
  > The option attribute name (e.g., 'color', 'size', 'material'). Represents
  > the type of variant option being specified.
- `value`
  > The option attribute value (e.g., 'Red', 'Large', 'Cotton'). The specific
  > choice for this variant option.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this variant option record was created. Set automatically
  > when the order is placed.

### `shopping_mall_order_shipment_items`

Junction table linking order shipments to order items, enabling sellers
to bundle multiple items from the same seller into a single shipment with
one tracking number.

This table implements the many-to-one relationship between shipments and
order items, where:
- A shipment can contain multiple order items (same seller bundling)
- An order item can belong to exactly one shipment (unique constraint)

When a seller creates a shipment and selects order items to ship, records
are created in this junction table. The shipment's carrier name and
tracking number apply to all bundled items.

Relationships:
- References [shopping_mall_order_shipments](#shopping_mall_order_shipments) for the shipment record
- References [shopping_mall_order_items](#shopping_mall_order_items) for the individual order
items

The unique constraint on order_item_id ensures each order item is shipped
exactly once, preventing duplicate shipment assignments.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_order_shipment_id`
  > Reference to the shipment that contains this order item. Links to {@link
  > shopping_mall_order_shipments.id} to associate the order item with
  > carrier and tracking information.
- `shopping_mall_order_item_id`
  > Reference to the order item being shipped. Links to {@link
  > shopping_mall_order_items.id}. Unique constraint ensures each order item
  > can only be assigned to one shipment.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the order item was assigned to this shipment. Records the
  > moment the seller included this item in the shipment.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this shipment item assignment was last modified. Typically
  > matches created_at as assignments are usually not modified after
  > creation.

### `shopping_mall_order_shipment_audit_logs`

Immutable audit trail for shipment lifecycle events capturing creation,
status transitions, delivery confirmations (both manual by customer and
automatic after 14 days), and administrative interventions. Each log
entry records the event type, previous and new status, responsible actor
(seller, customer, admin, or system), connection context (IP, URL), and
timestamp. Provides complete traceability for dispute resolution and
compliance. References [shopping_mall_order_shipments](#shopping_mall_order_shipments) for shipment
association.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_order_shipment_id`
  > Reference to the shipment being audited. {@link
  > shopping_mall_order_shipments.id}.
- `event_type`
  > Type of shipment lifecycle event. Values: 'created' (shipment created by
  > seller), 'status_changed' (manual status update), 'delivered_manually'
  > (customer confirmed delivery), 'delivered_auto' (automatic delivery after
  > 14 days), 'admin_override' (administrator intervention).
- `old_status`
  > Previous shipment status before the event. Null for 'created' events
  > which have no prior state. Values: 'preparing', 'shipped', 'delivered'.
- `new_status`
  > New shipment status after the event. Values: 'preparing' (initial),
  > 'shipped' (carrier has package), 'delivered' (received by customer).
- `actor_type`
  > Type of actor who performed the action. Values: 'seller' (merchant
  > shipping items), 'customer' (buyer confirming delivery), 'admin'
  > (administrator override), 'system' (automatic process for 14-day
  > delivery).
- `actor_id`
  > UUID of the actor who performed the action. References
  > shopping_mall_sellers.id, shopping_mall_customers.id, or
  > shopping_mall_admins.id based on actor_type. Null for 'system' actor
  > type.
- `ip`
  > IP address of the client that triggered the event. Used for security
  > audit and fraud detection. Null for system-triggered events.
- `href`
  > URL path of the API endpoint that triggered the event. Provides context
  > for understanding which operation caused the status change. Null for
  > system-triggered events.
- `notes`
  > Optional additional context or reason for the event. Used for admin
  > override explanations, automatic delivery confirmation details, or other
  > relevant information.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the audit log entry was created. Represents the exact
  > moment the shipment event occurred. Used for chronological ordering and
  > time-based analysis.

### `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`

Customer-initiated cancellation requests for order items with 'paid' status.

Customers can request cancellation for order items that have not yet been
shipped (status: paid). Each request captures the customer's reason,
tracks the approval workflow through pending/approved/rejected statuses,
and records seller responses including rejection reasons when applicable.

Key relationships:
- References [shopping_mall_order_items.id](#shopping_mall_order_items) for the item being
cancelled (1:1 - one request per item)
- References [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers) for the requesting customer
- Seller context is derived through the order item's seller association

Business rules:
- Only order items with 'paid' status can have cancellation requests
- Approved cancellations trigger automatic refund and stock restoration
- All state changes are captured in {@link
shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots} for audit

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `order_item_id`
  > The order item being cancelled. References {@link
  > shopping_mall_order_items.id}. Only one cancellation request allowed per
  > order item.
- `customer_id`
  > The customer who initiated the cancellation request. References {@link
  > shopping_mall_customers.id}.
- `reason`: Customer's explanation for why they want to cancel this order item.
- `status`
  > Current state of the cancellation request: pending (awaiting seller
  > review), approved (seller accepted, refund initiated), or rejected
  > (seller declined with reason provided).
- `seller_response`
  > Seller's response message when approving or rejecting the request.
  > Optional additional context from the seller.
- `rejection_reason`
  > Reason provided by seller when rejecting the cancellation request.
  > Required when status is 'rejected'.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the cancellation request was created.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the cancellation request was last modified (status change,
  > seller response, etc.).

### `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots`

Immutable snapshots preserving complete state of cancellation requests at
each stage of their lifecycle. Created automatically when a cancellation
request is submitted and when a seller responds (approve/reject). Records
the transition from previous status to new status, along with the
customer's reason for cancellation, seller's response, and rejection
reason if applicable. Provides complete audit trail for dispute
resolution and legal compliance as required by the snapshot principle.
Each snapshot represents a single state transition and cannot be modified
or deleted.

Related to [shopping_mall_cancellation_requests](#shopping_mall_cancellation_requests) for the parent
cancellation request entity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_id`
  > The cancellation request this snapshot captures. {@link
  > shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.id}
- `previous_status`
  > The status of the cancellation request before this state change. Null for
  > initial submission snapshots.
- `new_status`
  > The status of the cancellation request after this state change. Values:
  > 'pending' for initial submission, 'approved' when seller approves,
  > 'rejected' when seller rejects.
- `reason`
  > Customer's explanation for why they want to cancel the order item.
  > Captured at the time of snapshot creation to preserve the exact wording.
- `seller_response`
  > Seller's response or explanation when approving or rejecting the
  > cancellation request. Null for initial submission snapshots, populated
  > when seller responds.
- `rejection_reason`
  > Seller's explanation for rejecting the cancellation request. Null for
  > approved or pending statuses, populated only when seller rejects the
  > request.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this snapshot was created, representing when the state
  > transition occurred.

### `shopping_mall_reviews`

Customer reviews and ratings for purchased products, containing rating
(1-5 stars), optional text content, and references to customer, product,
and order for purchase verification.

Supports soft delete to preserve reviews when customers delete accounts,
displaying as 'deleted user' while maintaining review content for product
rating calculations. Enforces one review per product per order constraint
to prevent duplicate reviews.

Reviews can only be written for delivered order items. When customers
edit their reviews, snapshots are created separately in {@link
shopping_mall_review_snapshots} for audit trails and dispute resolution.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`
  > Customer who wrote this review. Referenced as 'deleted user' when
  > customer account is deleted. References {@link
  > shopping_mall_customers.id}.
- `product_id`
  > Product being reviewed. Used for product-level rating calculation and
  > filtering. References [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products).
- `order_id`
  > Order through which the product was purchased. Used for purchase
  > verification and enforcing one-review-per-product-per-order constraint.
  > References [shopping_mall_orders.id](#shopping_mall_orders).
- `rating`
  > Rating value from 1 to 5 stars. Required for all reviews. Used to
  > calculate product average rating.
- `content`
  > Optional text content of the review. Supports full-text search via GIN
  > index. Maximum 2000 characters.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the review was created.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the review was last updated. Used for snapshot creation
  > triggers.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp. When set, review is hidden from display but
  > preserved for rating calculations and audit. Used when customer deletes
  > account - review displays as 'deleted user'.

### `shopping_mall_review_snapshots`

Immutable snapshot records of review edits preserving previous and new
rating values and text content. Created automatically when customers
modify their reviews to maintain complete edit history for dispute
resolution and audit purposes.

Each snapshot captures the state transition from previous to new values,
recording when the change occurred and what values changed. Snapshots are
never deleted even if the parent review is soft-deleted, ensuring
permanent audit trails for the snapshot principle.

Supports the platform's financial accountability model where customer
feedback disputes may require historical evidence of what was originally
written versus current state.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_review_id`: The review that was edited. References [shopping_mall_reviews.id](#shopping_mall_reviews).
- `previous_rating`
  > The rating value (1-5 stars) before this edit was made. Captures the
  > previous state for audit comparison.
- `new_rating`
  > The rating value (1-5 stars) after this edit was made. Captures the new
  > state for audit comparison.
- `previous_content`
  > The text content before this edit was made. Null if the review had no
  > text content originally.
- `new_content`
  > The text content after this edit was made. Null if the customer removed
  > all text content.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this snapshot was created, coinciding with when the review
  > edit was submitted.

text: I'll now execute the Interface agent to create the API interface specification. This will generate OpenAPI schemas and NestJS controller/DTO definitions based on the database schema and requirements.

instruction:
Create API interfaces for an e-commerce shopping mall platform with the following endpoints:

**Customer Authentication APIs:**
- POST /api/auth/customers/signup - Customer registration (email, password, displayName, phone)
- POST /api/auth/customers/login - Customer login (email, password) returns JWT token
- PUT /api/auth/customers/password - Change password (requires authentication)
- DELETE /api/auth/customers/account - Delete account (requires authentication)

**Customer Profile APIs:**
- GET /api/customers/me - Get current customer profile
- PUT /api/customers/me - Update profile (displayName, phone)

**Address Management APIs:**
- GET /api/customers/me/addresses - List all addresses
- POST /api/customers/me/addresses - Add new address
- PUT /api/customers/me/addresses/:id - Update address
- DELETE /api/customers/me/addresses/:id - Delete address
- PUT /api/customers/me/addresses/:id/default - Set as default address

**Seller Authentication APIs:**
- POST /api/auth/sellers/signup - Seller registration (email, password, shopName, shopDescription, logoUrl)
- POST /api/auth/sellers/login - Seller login returns JWT token
- PUT /api/auth/sellers/password - Change password
- DELETE /api/auth/sellers/account - Delete account (only if no pending orders/refunds)
- GET /api/auth/sellers/approval-status - View approval status

**Seller Profile APIs:**
- GET /api/sellers/me - Get own seller profile
- PUT /api/sellers/me - Update shop profile (shopName, shopDescription, logoUrl)
- GET /api/sellers/:id - Public seller profile view (for customers)

**Category APIs:**
- GET /api/categories - List all categories (public)
- GET /api/categories/:id/products - Products in category (public, paginated)
- POST /api/admin/categories - Create category (admin only)
- PUT /api/admin/categories/:id - Update category (admin only)
- DELETE /api/admin/categories/:id - Delete category (admin only)

**Product APIs (Public):**
- GET /api/products - Search products with filters (name, category, priceRange, inStock, sort, page)
- GET /api/products/:id - Product detail with variants, images, seller info, reviews

**Product APIs (Seller):**
- POST /api/sellers/me/products - Create product (name, description, categoryId, basePrice)
- PUT /api/sellers/me/products/:id - Update product
- DELETE /api/sellers/me/products/:id - Delete product (only if no pending orders)
- GET /api/sellers/me/products/:id/snapshots - View product snapshots

**Product Image APIs:**
- POST /api/sellers/me/products/:id/images - Upload product images (multipart)
- DELETE /api/sellers/me/products/:id/images/:imageId - Delete image
- PUT /api/sellers/me/products/:id/images/reorder - Reorder images

**Product Variant APIs:**
- POST /api/sellers/me/products/:id/variants - Add variant (skuCode, optionValues, priceOverride, stockQuantity)
- PUT /api/sellers/me/products/:id/variants/:variantId - Update variant
- DELETE /api/sellers/me/products/:id/variants/:variantId - Delete variant (only if no pending orders)

**Inventory APIs:**
- POST /api/sellers/me/variants/:id/inventory/add - Add inventory (quantity, reason)
- POST /api/sellers/me/variants/:id/inventory/subtract - Subtract inventory (quantity, reason)
- GET /api/sellers/me/variants/:id/inventory/history - View inventory history

**Wishlist APIs:**
- GET /api/customers/me/wishlist - View wishlist (paginated)
- POST /api/customers/me/wishlist - Add product to wishlist (productId)
- DELETE /api/customers/me/wishlist/:productId - Remove from wishlist

**Shopping Cart APIs:**
- GET /api/customers/me/cart - View cart with unavailable item warnings
- POST /api/customers/me/cart - Add variant to cart (variantId, quantity)
- PUT /api/customers/me/cart/:itemId - Update quantity
- DELETE /api/customers/me/cart/:itemId - Remove from cart

**Checkout & Order APIs:**
- POST /api/customers/me/checkout/prepare - Prepare checkout (validate cart, return order summary)
- POST /api/customers/me/orders - Place order (addressId, payment info) returns orderId
- GET /api/customers/me/orders - Order history (paginated, sorted newest first)
- GET /api/customers/me/orders/:id - Order detail with items and shipments

**Shipment APIs (Seller):**
- GET /api/sellers/me/order-items - List order items to ship (filter by status)
- POST /api/sellers/me/shipments - Create shipment (orderItemIds, carrierName, trackingNumber)

**Shipment APIs (Customer):**
- GET /api/customers/me/orders/:orderId/shipments - View shipments
- POST /api/customers/me/shipments/:id/confirm-delivery - Confirm delivery

**Cancellation APIs:**
- POST /api/customers/me/order-items/:id/cancellation - Request cancellation (reason)
- PUT /api/sellers/me/cancellations/:id/approve - Approve cancellation
- PUT /api/sellers/me/cancellations/:id/reject - Reject cancellation

**Refund APIs:**
- POST /api/customers/me/order-items/:id/refund - Request refund (reason)
- PUT /api/sellers/me/refunds/:id/approve - Approve refund
- PUT /api/sellers/me/refunds/:id/reject - Reject refund

**Review APIs:**
- POST /api/customers/me/reviews - Create review (productId, orderId, rating, content)
- PUT /api/customers/me/reviews/:id - Edit review
- DELETE /api/customers/me/reviews/:id - Delete review

**Seller Dashboard APIs:**
- GET /api/sellers/me/dashboard - Summary (productCount, orderItemCount, pendingCancellations, pendingRefunds)
- GET /api/sellers/me/order-items - List order items with filters

**Administrator Request APIs:**
- POST /api/admin-requests - Submit admin request (reason)
- GET /api/admin/admin-requests - List pending requests (super admin only)
- PUT /api/admin/admin-requests/:id/approve - Approve request
- PUT /api/admin/admin-requests/:id/reject - Reject request

**Administrator Management APIs:**
- PUT /api/admin/promote/:id - Promote to super admin (super admin only)
- PUT /api/admin/demote/:id - Demote to regular admin (super admin only)

**Seller Approval APIs (Admin):**
- GET /api/admin/seller-approvals - List pending seller approvals
- PUT /api/admin/seller-approvals/:id/approve - Approve seller
- PUT /api/admin/seller-approvals/:id/reject - Reject seller (requires reason)

**Seller Management APIs (Admin):**
- PUT /api/admin/sellers/:id/suspend - Suspend seller
- PUT /api/admin/sellers/:id/unsuspend - Unsuspend seller
- PUT /api/admin/sellers/:id/ban - Ban seller
- PUT /api/admin/sellers/:id/unban - Unban seller

**Product Oversight APIs (Admin):**
- GET /api/admin/products - View all products (paginated)
- GET /api/admin/products/:id/snapshots - View product snapshots
- DELETE /api/admin/products/:id - Delete product (policy violation)

**Order Oversight APIs (Admin):**
- GET /api/admin/orders - View all orders (paginated)
- POST /api/admin/orders/:id/force-cancel - Force cancel order (refunds customer, restores stock)
- POST /api/admin/orders/:id/force-refund - Force refund order

**Customer Management APIs (Admin):**
- GET /api/admin/customers - View all customers
- PUT /api/admin/customers/:id/ban - Ban customer
- PUT /api/admin/customers/:id/unban - Unban customer

**Snapshot APIs:**
- GET /api/sellers/me/products/:id/snapshots - Seller views own product snapshots
- GET /api/admin/products/:id/snapshots - Admin views any product snapshots

**Authentication & Authorization:**
- JWT Bearer token authentication
- Role-based access control (CUSTOMER, SELLER, ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN)
- Some endpoints public (product browsing, categories, seller profiles)
- Seller endpoints require approved seller status
- Admin endpoints require admin role

operations.specification:
Create a new customer account in the e-commerce platform.

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Validate request body - email must be unique, password must meet complexity requirements
2. Hash password using bcrypt with appropriate salt rounds
3. Create customer record in shopping_mall_customers table with email, password_hash, display_name (optional), phone_number (optional)
4. Generate JWT tokens - access_token (30 min) and refresh_token (14 days)
5. Create session record in shopping_mall_customer_sessions table with tokens, IP, user agent
6. Return IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized response with both tokens

**Validation Rules:**
- Email: required, valid email format, must be unique across all customers
- Password: required, minimum 8 characters, should include complexity rules
- displayName: optional, max 100 characters
- phone: optional, valid phone format

**Database Operations:**
- INSERT into shopping_mall_customers
- INSERT into shopping_mall_customer_sessions

**Error Handling:**
- 409 Conflict: Email already exists
- 400 Bad Request: Invalid input data
operations.description:
Registers a new customer account on the e-commerce shopping mall platform.

This endpoint creates a new customer account with email and password credentials. The email must be unique across all customer accounts in the system. Upon successful registration, the customer receives JWT tokens for immediate authentication.

The request body accepts email (required), password (required), displayName (optional), and phone (optional). The password is securely hashed using bcrypt before storage in the shopping_mall_customers table.

Upon successful registration, the system automatically creates an authentication session record in shopping_mall_customer_sessions containing the access token (30-minute expiration) and refresh token (14-day expiration), along with connection metadata (IP address, user agent) for security tracking.

The response returns an IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized object containing the access token, refresh token, and basic customer information. These tokens enable the customer to immediately access authenticated endpoints without requiring a separate login.

**Security Considerations:**
- Password is hashed with bcrypt before storage (never stored in plain text)
- Session tokens are unique and tracked for multi-device support
- Email uniqueness is enforced to prevent duplicate accounts

requestBody.description: Customer registration details including email, password, and optional profile information (displayName, phone).

responseBody.description: JWT authentication tokens and customer information upon successful registration.

Authenticate an existing customer and create a new session.

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Validate request body - email and password are required
2. Find customer by email in shopping_mall_customers table
3. Verify password_hash using bcrypt.compare()
4. Check if customer is deleted (deleted_at is null)
5. Generate new JWT tokens - access_token (30 min) and refresh_token (14 days)
6. Create session record in shopping_mall_customer_sessions table
7. Return IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized response with both tokens

**Validation Rules:**
- Email: required, valid email format
- Password: required

**Database Operations:**
- SELECT from shopping_mall_customers WHERE email = ?
- INSERT into shopping_mall_customer_sessions

**Error Handling:**
- 401 Unauthorized: Invalid email or password
- 403 Forbidden: Account is deleted
- 400 Bad Request: Invalid input data
operations.description:
Authenticates an existing customer using email and password credentials.

This endpoint validates customer credentials against the shopping_mall_customers table. The email serves as the unique identifier, and the password is verified against the stored bcrypt hash. Upon successful authentication, a new session is created.

The request body requires email and password. The system checks that the account exists, is active (not soft-deleted), and that the password matches the stored hash.

Upon successful login, the system creates a new authentication session record in shopping_mall_customer_sessions containing:
- access_token: Short-lived JWT (30-minute expiration) for API authentication
- refresh_token: Long-lived JWT (14-day expiration) for token renewal
- Connection metadata: IP address, user agent, href, referrer for device tracking

The response returns an IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized object with both tokens and customer information. These tokens should be stored securely by the client (typically in httpOnly cookies or secure localStorage).

**Multi-Device Support:**
Multiple sessions can exist simultaneously for the same customer, enabling login from multiple devices. Each session is independently tracked and can be revoked.

**Security Considerations:**
- Password verification uses constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks
- Deleted accounts (deleted_at not null) cannot authenticate
- Session tokens are unique per login, not reused

requestBody.description: Customer login credentials including email and password.

responseBody.description: JWT authentication tokens and customer information upon successful login.

operations.specification:
Refresh an expired access token using a valid refresh token.

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Validate request body - refresh_token is required
2. Find session by refresh_token in shopping_mall_customer_sessions table
3. Verify session has not expired (expired_at > now)
4. Get associated customer from shopping_mall_customers
5. Verify customer is not deleted (deleted_at is null)
6. Generate new JWT tokens - new access_token (30 min) and refresh_token (14 days)
7. Update session record with new tokens and extended expiration
8. Return IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized response with new tokens

**Validation Rules:**
- refresh_token: required, must exist in database, must not be expired

**Database Operations:**
- SELECT from shopping_mall_customer_sessions WHERE refresh_token = ?
- SELECT from shopping_mall_customers WHERE id = ?
- UPDATE shopping_mall_customer_sessions SET access_token, refresh_token, expired_at

**Error Handling:**
- 401 Unauthorized: Invalid or expired refresh token
- 403 Forbidden: Account is deleted
- 400 Bad Request: Invalid input data
operations.description:
Renews authentication tokens using a valid refresh token.

This endpoint allows customers to obtain new access and refresh tokens without re-entering credentials. The refresh token is exchanged for a fresh set of tokens, enabling seamless continued access.

The request body requires refresh_token - the long-lived token received during login or previous refresh. The system validates that the token exists in shopping_mall_customer_sessions and has not expired (expired_at is in the future).

Upon successful validation, the system:
1. Generates a new access_token (30-minute expiration)
2. Generates a new refresh_token (14-day expiration from now)
3. Updates the session record with the new tokens
4. Extends the session expiration date

The response returns an IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized object with the new tokens. The old tokens become invalid after refresh.

**Token Rotation:**
Each refresh generates completely new tokens. The old refresh token is replaced, not extended. This rotation pattern enhances security by limiting the window of vulnerability if tokens are compromised.

**Session Continuity:**
The session record is updated in place rather than creating a new session, maintaining session continuity and preserving connection metadata from the original login.

**Security Considerations:**
- Expired refresh tokens require re-authentication
- Deleted accounts cannot refresh tokens
- Token rotation prevents token reuse attacks

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining new access token.

responseBody.description: New JWT authentication tokens and customer information upon successful refresh.

operations.description:
Registers a new seller account on the e-commerce platform.

This endpoint handles seller registration by collecting essential account information including email address, password, and shop profile details. Upon successful registration, the seller account is created with approval_status set to 'pending', requiring administrator review before the seller can operate on the platform.

The email field must be unique across all seller accounts. The password is securely hashed using bcrypt before storage. Shop profile information (shop_name, shop_description, logo_url) is captured at registration but can be modified later.

Security considerations: Password is never stored in plain text. Email uniqueness validation prevents duplicate accounts. The pending status prevents unauthorized sellers from listing products immediately.

Related operations: After registration, sellers must wait for admin approval (GET /auth/seller/approval-status) before accessing seller features. Once approved, sellers can login via POST /auth/seller/login.

The operation does NOT create a session since pending sellers cannot access seller features until approved by administrator.

operations.description:
Authenticates a seller and creates a new session with JWT tokens.

This endpoint validates seller credentials (email and password) and issues JWT tokens for API authentication. The response includes both an access token for API requests and a refresh token for session renewal. Multi-device sessions are supported through device tracking.

The login process validates the approval_status before allowing access: pending accounts receive an approval-required error, rejected accounts see their rejection reason, and suspended accounts are denied access. Only approved sellers can successfully login.

Security considerations: Failed login attempts should be rate-limited. Device context (IP, referrer) is logged for security auditing. Password validation uses secure bcrypt comparison. Session tokens are unique and cannot be reused.

Related operations: Use POST /auth/seller/refresh to renew tokens before expiration. Session information can be managed through session management endpoints.
operations.name: login

requestBody.description: Seller login credentials for authentication.

responseBody.description: JWT tokens and seller profile information for authenticated session.

operations.specification: Implementation requires: 1) Query shopping_mall_sellers table for matching email; 2) Validate password by comparing bcrypt hash of input against stored password_hash; 3) Check approval_status - if 'pending', return error indicating approval required; if 'rejected', return error with rejection_reason; if 'suspended', return error indicating account suspended; 4) Generate JWT access_token (15-30 min expiration) and refresh_token (7-30 days expiration); 5) Create shopping_mall_seller_sessions record with seller_id, tokens, device context (ip from request, href, referrer, device_name from headers), and expiration timestamps; 6) Return tokens with seller profile information.

operations.description:
Renews authentication tokens using a valid refresh token.

This endpoint allows sellers to obtain new access and refresh tokens without re-entering credentials. The refresh token from a previous login or refresh operation is exchanged for a new token pair, extending the session seamlessly.

The operation validates that the refresh token exists in the sessions table and hasn't expired. The associated seller account must still have 'approved' status to receive new tokens. Expired refresh tokens require re-authentication through the login endpoint.

Security considerations: Each refresh generates new tokens and invalidates the previous refresh token, preventing token reuse attacks. Session expiration is extended with each refresh, up to the maximum session lifetime. Device context is preserved from the original login session.

Related operations: This endpoint is called automatically by clients when the access token approaches expiration. Full re-authentication via POST /auth/seller/login is required if the refresh token expires or becomes invalid.
operations.name: refresh

requestBody.description: Valid refresh token from previous authentication.

responseBody.description: New JWT tokens and seller profile information for continued session.

operations.specification: Implementation requires: 1) Validate the refresh_token format and integrity; 2) Query shopping_mall_seller_sessions table to find session with matching refresh_token; 3) Check if session has expired (expired_at > current time); 4) If valid, retrieve the associated shopping_mall_sellers record; 5) Verify seller approval_status is still 'approved'; 6) Generate new access_token and refresh_token pair; 7) Update the session record with new tokens and extended expiration; 8) Return new tokens with seller profile. If refresh_token is invalid or expired, return 401 Unauthorized.

The system validates email uniqueness before creation. A refresh token is generated and stored in shopping_mall_admin_sessions with device context (IP, href, referrer) for audit purposes. The response includes both access and refresh tokens.

This endpoint registers a new administrator account for the e-commerce platform management system.

Administrator accounts provide elevated permissions for platform oversight including seller approval, category management, product oversight, order management, and user moderation. New administrators are created with 'regular' grade by default - super administrator status must be granted by an existing super administrator through a separate promotion process.

- Display name for identification in admin panels and audit logs

Related operations: After joining, administrators can login (/auth/admin/login) to establish new sessions and refresh (/auth/admin/refresh) to renew tokens.

operations.description:
This endpoint renews authentication tokens for an administrator session using a valid refresh token.

JWT tokens have limited lifespans for security: access tokens expire in 15-30 minutes, refresh tokens in 7-30 days. When an access token expires, clients use this endpoint to obtain new tokens without requiring the administrator to re-enter credentials.

The refresh process:
1. Validates the refresh token signature and expiration
2. Verifies the associated session has not expired in shopping_mall_admin_sessions
3. Issues new access and refresh tokens
4. Invalidates the old refresh token to prevent replay attacks
5. Updates session timestamps for activity tracking

This endpoint enables seamless user experience by maintaining authentication across extended sessions while preserving security through token rotation and expiration enforcement.

Related operations: After initial authentication via login (/auth/admin/login), tokens can be refreshed periodically. If refresh token expires, the administrator must login again.

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens and current administrator profile information.

operations.specification:
Create a new customer account in the e-commerce platform.

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Validate request body - email must be unique, password must meet complexity requirements
2. Hash password using bcrypt with appropriate salt rounds
3. Create customer record in shopping_mall_customers table with email, password_hash, display_name (optional), phone_number (optional)
4. Generate JWT tokens - access_token (30 min) and refresh_token (14 days)
5. Create session record in shopping_mall_customer_sessions table with tokens, IP, user agent
6. Return IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized response with both tokens

**Validation Rules:**
- Email: required, valid email format, must be unique across all customers
- Password: required, minimum 8 characters, should include complexity rules
- displayName: optional, max 100 characters
- phone: optional, valid phone format

**Database Operations:**
- INSERT into shopping_mall_customers
- INSERT into shopping_mall_customer_sessions

**Error Handling:**
- 409 Conflict: Email already exists
- 400 Bad Request: Invalid input data
operations.description:
Registers a new customer account on the e-commerce shopping mall platform.

This endpoint creates a new customer account with email and password credentials. The email must be unique across all customer accounts in the system. Upon successful registration, the customer receives JWT tokens for immediate authentication.

The request body accepts email (required), password (required), displayName (optional), and phone (optional). The password is securely hashed using bcrypt before storage in the shopping_mall_customers table.

Upon successful registration, the system automatically creates an authentication session record in shopping_mall_customer_sessions containing the access token (30-minute expiration) and refresh token (14-day expiration), along with connection metadata (IP address, user agent) for security tracking.

The response returns an IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized object containing the access token, refresh token, and basic customer information. These tokens enable the customer to immediately access authenticated endpoints without requiring a separate login.

**Security Considerations:**
- Password is hashed with bcrypt before storage (never stored in plain text)
- Session tokens are unique and tracked for multi-device support
- Email uniqueness is enforced to prevent duplicate accounts

requestBody.description: Customer registration details including email, password, and optional profile information (displayName, phone).

responseBody.description: JWT authentication tokens and customer information upon successful registration.

Authenticate an existing customer and create a new session.

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Validate request body - email and password are required
2. Find customer by email in shopping_mall_customers table
3. Verify password_hash using bcrypt.compare()
4. Check if customer is deleted (deleted_at is null)
5. Generate new JWT tokens - access_token (30 min) and refresh_token (14 days)
6. Create session record in shopping_mall_customer_sessions table
7. Return IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized response with both tokens

**Validation Rules:**
- Email: required, valid email format
- Password: required

**Database Operations:**
- SELECT from shopping_mall_customers WHERE email = ?
- INSERT into shopping_mall_customer_sessions

**Error Handling:**
- 401 Unauthorized: Invalid email or password

operations.description:
Authenticates an existing customer using email and password credentials.

This endpoint validates customer credentials against the shopping_mall_customers table. The email serves as the unique identifier, and the password is verified against the stored bcrypt hash. Upon successful authentication, a new session is created.

The request body requires email and password. The system checks that the account exists, is active (not soft-deleted), and that the password matches the stored hash.

Upon successful login, the system creates a new authentication session record in shopping_mall_customer_sessions containing:
- access_token: Short-lived JWT (30-minute expiration) for API authentication
- refresh_token: Long-lived JWT (14-day expiration) for token renewal
- Connection metadata: IP address, user agent, href, referrer for device tracking

The response returns an IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized object with both tokens and customer information. These tokens should be stored securely by the client (typically in httpOnly cookies or secure localStorage).

**Multi-Device Support:**
Multiple sessions can exist simultaneously for the same customer, enabling login from multiple devices. Each session is independently tracked and can be revoked.

**Security Considerations:**
- Password verification uses constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks
- Deleted accounts (deleted_at not null) cannot authenticate
- Session tokens are unique per login, not reused

requestBody.description: Customer login credentials including email and password.

responseBody.description: JWT authentication tokens and customer information upon successful login.

operations.specification:
Refresh an expired access token using a valid refresh token.

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Validate request body - refresh_token is required
2. Find session by refresh_token in shopping_mall_customer_sessions table
3. Verify session has not expired (expired_at > now)
4. Get associated customer from shopping_mall_customers
5. Verify customer is not deleted (deleted_at is null)
6. Generate new JWT tokens - new access_token (30 min) and refresh_token (14 days)
7. Update session record with new tokens and extended expiration
8. Return IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized response with new tokens

**Validation Rules:**
- refresh_token: required, must exist in database, must not be expired

**Database Operations:**
- SELECT from shopping_mall_customer_sessions WHERE refresh_token = ?
- SELECT from shopping_mall_customers WHERE id = ?
- UPDATE shopping_mall_customer_sessions SET access_token, refresh_token, expired_at

**Error Handling:**
- 401 Unauthorized: Invalid or expired refresh token
- 403 Forbidden: Account is deleted
- 400 Bad Request: Invalid input data
operations.description:
Renews authentication tokens using a valid refresh token.

This endpoint allows customers to obtain new access and refresh tokens without re-entering credentials. The refresh token is exchanged for a fresh set of tokens, enabling seamless continued access.

The request body requires refresh_token - the long-lived token received during login or previous refresh. The system validates that the token exists in shopping_mall_customer_sessions and has not expired (expired_at is in the future).

Upon successful validation, the system:
1. Generates a new access_token (30-minute expiration)
2. Generates a new refresh_token (14-day expiration from now)
3. Updates the session record with the new tokens
4. Extends the session expiration date

The response returns an IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized object with the new tokens. The old tokens become invalid after refresh.

**Token Rotation:**
Each refresh generates completely new tokens. The old refresh token is replaced, not extended. This rotation pattern enhances security by limiting the window of vulnerability if tokens are compromised.

**Session Continuity:**
The session record is updated in place rather than creating a new session, maintaining session continuity and preserving connection metadata from the original login.

**Security Considerations:**
- Expired refresh tokens require re-authentication
- Deleted accounts cannot refresh tokens
- Token rotation prevents token reuse attacks

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining new access token.

responseBody.description: New JWT authentication tokens and customer information upon successful refresh.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of customer accounts for administrative oversight.

This endpoint provides administrators with comprehensive customer search capabilities, enabling efficient management and monitoring of the platform's customer base. Administrators can search by email address, display name (with partial matching support), phone number, registration date range, and account deletion status.

The search leverages database indexes for optimal performance: unique index on email for exact/partial email matching, and GIN trigram index on display_name for efficient fuzzy text search. Results are paginated to handle large customer bases efficiently.

**Filtering Options:**
- Email: Partial matching supported (case-insensitive)
- Display Name: Full-text search with trigram matching for typo tolerance
- Phone Number: Partial matching supported
- Registration Date Range: Filter by created_at timestamp
- Account Status: Filter by active/deleted accounts

**Sorting Options:**
- Newest first (default): created_at DESC
- Oldest first: created_at ASC
- Email alphabetical: email ASC/DESC

**Security Considerations:**
- Requires administrator authentication
- Sensitive data (password hashes) never exposed
- Soft-deleted accounts included by default, can be filtered
- Customer PII is accessible only to administrators

**Related Operations:**
- Use GET /customers/{customerId} to view detailed customer information
- Use PUT /admin/customers/{id}/ban to ban a customer
- Use PUT /admin/customers/{id}/unban to restore customer access
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_customers table with pagination, filtering, and sorting support.

**Database Query Logic:**
1. Build WHERE clause from request filters:
   - email: ILIKE '%{email}%' for case-insensitive partial match
   - displayName: Use text search with GIN trigram index for efficient fuzzy matching
   - phoneNumber: ILIKE '%{phoneNumber}%' for partial match
   - createdFrom/createdTo: created_at BETWEEN range filter
   - isDeleted: If true, filter deleted_at IS NOT NULL; if false, filter deleted_at IS NULL; if null, include all
2. Apply ORDER BY based on sort parameter (default: created_at DESC)
3. Execute COUNT query for total count
4. Execute SELECT query with OFFSET/LIMIT for pagination
5. Transform results to ISummary format excluding sensitive fields

**Performance Considerations:**
- Use database indexes: @@unique([email]), @@index([display_name(ops: gin_trgm_ops)])
- Avoid SELECT *; select only fields needed for summary
- Consider cursor-based pagination for very large result sets in future optimization

**Edge Cases:**
- Empty filter criteria returns all customers (subject to pagination limits)
- Invalid date range returns validation error
- Negative page number defaults to page 1
- Excessive page size capped at 100

**Response Transformation:**
- Map id, email, displayName, phoneNumber, createdAt, updatedAt
- Map deleted_at to isDeleted boolean
- Calculate derived fields if needed (e.g., order count would require separate query)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of customer account summaries

requestBody.description: Customer search criteria with pagination and sorting options

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific customer account.

This admin-only endpoint allows administrators to view complete customer profile information including email address, display name, phone number, and account timestamps. This information supports administrative oversight functions such as reviewing account details before taking moderation actions like banning or unbanning a customer.

The response includes the customer's current profile state. If the customer has been soft-deleted (deleted_at is set), the record still exists but the profile information may have been cleared per data preservation policies. When a customer deletes their account, their display_name and phone_number are cleared, but orders and reviews are preserved for legal compliance.

**Security Considerations:**
This endpoint is restricted to administrator access only. The password_hash field is never exposed in the response for security reasons. Administrators can use this information to verify customer identity when handling support requests or investigating account-related issues.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_customers table by primary key (id) to retrieve a single customer record.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate the customerId path parameter as a valid UUID format
2. Query shopping_mall_customers table WHERE id = customerId
3. If no record found, return 404 Not Found error
4. Exclude password_hash field from the response for security
5. Return the customer object with fields: id, email, display_name, phone_number, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at

Note: The deleted_at field will be null for active accounts and set to a timestamp for soft-deleted accounts. When soft-deleted, display_name and phone_number may be null per data preservation rules.

responseBody.description: Customer account details including profile information and timestamps

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the customer to retrieve
parameters.name: customerId

operations.description:
Update the authenticated customer's profile information.

This operation allows customers to modify their optional profile fields: display name shown in reviews and order communications, and phone number for delivery coordination. Both fields are optional and can be set, changed, or cleared independently.

**Display Name Usage:**
- Shown as author name in product reviews
- Used in order communication notifications
- Displayed as 'Customer' if not set

**Phone Number Usage:**
- Used for delivery coordination
- Contact for shipping notifications

**Validation Rules:**
- Display name: Maximum 100 characters, cannot contain profanity or impersonate admin/seller
- Phone number: Valid international format (E.164), maximum 20 characters

The operation updates the profile atomically and records the update timestamp. Customers can only update their own profile.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update customer profile fields in shopping_mall_customers table.

1. Authenticate customer from JWT token
2. Validate request body fields:
   - displayName: If provided, check max length (100), check for profanity filter, check for reserved terms (admin, seller)
   - phoneNumber: If provided, validate E.164 format, max length (20)
3. Update customer record:
   - SET display_name = request.displayName (can be null to clear)
   - SET phone_number = request.phoneNumber (can be null to clear)
   - SET updated_at = NOW()
4. Return updated customer profile (excluding password_hash)

Business rules:
- Customer can only update their own profile
- Both fields are optional - can update one or both
- Setting field to null clears the value
- No snapshot required for profile updates (only for seller profiles)

responseBody.description: Updated customer profile information

requestBody.description: Profile update data with optional display name and phone number

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of active login sessions for the currently authenticated customer.

This endpoint enables customers to view all their active sessions across different devices, supporting multi-device session management. Customers can identify sessions by IP address, device information (via user agent), creation time, and expiration time. This information is essential for security awareness and session management, including the ability to identify potentially unauthorized access.

Sessions are stored in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table and are automatically filtered to only show records that belong to the authenticated customer. Expired sessions may optionally be included or excluded via the 'expired' filter parameter. The response includes pagination data to handle customers with many active sessions.

The response includes session metadata (id, IP, href, referrer, user agent, timestamps) but excludes access_token and refresh_token for security reasons.

Related operations: DELETE /shoppingMall/customer/sessions/{sessionId} for terminating a specific session, DELETE /shoppingMall/customer/sessions for logging out from all devices.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the appropriate session table based on JWT actor type:
- For 'customer' actor: SELECT from shopping_mall_customer_sessions WHERE shopping_mall_customer_id = ?
- For 'seller' actor: SELECT from shopping_mall_seller_sessions WHERE shopping_mall_seller_id = ?
- For 'admin' actor: SELECT from shopping_mall_admin_sessions WHERE shopping_mall_admin_id = ?

Apply filters:
- ip: ILIKE pattern match on ip column
- deviceName: ILIKE match on user_agent (customer) or device_name (seller) or skip for admin
- createdFrom/createdTo: filter on created_at range
- expired: if false, filter where expired_at > NOW()

Support pagination with cursor or offset-based approach. Order by created_at DESC by default.

Return session records with id, device info, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at. Exclude access_token and refresh_token from response for security.

Handle edge cases:
- Empty result set returns valid IPage with empty data array
- Invalid filter values return validation errors

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific authentication session.

This endpoint allows administrators to view session details for security auditing, device management, and suspicious activity detection purposes. Sessions can belong to customers, sellers, or administrators, and contain metadata such as IP address, user agent, device information, and timestamps.

The session information includes the actor type (customer, seller, or admin), connection metadata like IP address and referrer, device identification via user agent, and session lifecycle timestamps (creation and expiration). Access tokens are not exposed directly in the response for security reasons, but the session validity can be determined from the expiration timestamp.

This operation supports the platform's security and audit requirements by enabling administrators to investigate sessions for suspicious activity patterns, manage multi-device access, and maintain accountability for all authenticated actions.
operations.name: at

Query the appropriate session table based on the sessionId provided. The system must determine which session type (customer, seller, or admin) the ID belongs to by checking each session table.

2. If not found, check shopping_mall_seller_sessions where id = sessionId
3. If not found, check shopping_mall_admin_sessions where id = sessionId
4. If not found in any table, return 404 Not Found

Join with the respective actor table (shopping_mall_customers, shopping_mall_sellers, or shopping_mall_admins) to include actor information in the response.

The response should include:
- Session ID
- Actor type (customer, seller, admin)
- Actor summary (ID, email)
- IP address from login
- href and referrer from login request
- User agent / device name
- Created at timestamp
- Expired at timestamp
- Session validity status (current time < expired_at)

Security considerations:
- Do not expose access_token or refresh_token values in the response
- Log the admin's access to this session information for audit trail

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of products in the authenticated customer's wishlist.

This operation allows customers to view all products they have saved for future consideration. The wishlist tracks products at the product level (not specific variants), enabling customers to monitor items of interest without committing to a particular variant combination.

**Authentication Required:**
This endpoint requires customer authentication. Only the authenticated customer's own wishlist entries are returned. Attempting to access without authentication will result in a 401 Unauthorized error.

**Wishlist Behavior:**
- Maximum of 200 products per customer wishlist (enforced during add operation)
- Entries are automatically removed when referenced products are deleted by sellers
- Each customer-product pair can have exactly one wishlist entry
- Products display base price; variant-specific pricing shown on product detail page

**Response Structure:**
Each wishlist item includes product summary information (name, base price, seller shop name) and the timestamp when the product was added to the wishlist. The response supports pagination with configurable page sizes.

**Related Operations:**
- POST /wishlists - Add a product to the wishlist
- DELETE /wishlists/{productId} - Remove a product from the wishlist
- GET /products/{productId} - View detailed product information including all variants

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for wishlist items

responseBody.description: Paginated list of wishlist items with product summaries

operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_wishlists table filtered by the authenticated customer's ID from the JWT token.

**Database Query:**
1. Extract customer_id from authenticated session
2. Query shopping_mall_wishlists where customer_id matches
3. Join with shopping_mall_products to retrieve product details
4. Apply optional search filters if provided in request body (e.g., product name search, date range filter)
5. Support pagination with limit and offset/cursor parameters
6. Order by created_at descending (newest wishlist entries first)

**Product Information to Include:**
- Product id, name, base_price
- Seller shop name (from shopping_mall_sellers via product relationship)
- Main product image (first image from shopping_mall_product_images)
- Wishlist entry created_at timestamp
- Product availability status (deleted products are automatically removed via CASCADE)

**Edge Cases:**
- If product has no variants with stock, indicate as 'out of stock' in response
- Handle deleted products gracefully (entries removed automatically by database CASCADE)
- Return empty array if customer has no wishlist entries

**Performance Considerations:**
- Use efficient JOINs between wishlists, products, and sellers tables
- Consider adding database index on customer_id + created_at for pagination
- Limit maximum page size to prevent excessive data retrieval

operations.description:
Add a product to the authenticated customer's wishlist.

This operation allows authenticated customers to save products they are interested in for later viewing. The wishlist tracks products at the product level, not specific variants, allowing customers to select variants when they decide to purchase.

**Database Relationships:**
The shopping_mall_wishlists table maintains a foreign key relationship to shopping_mall_products with CASCADE DELETE, meaning wishlist entries are automatically removed when the referenced product is deleted by the seller.

**Authentication Required:** This endpoint requires a valid customer JWT token. The customer ID is automatically extracted from the authentication context.

**Business Rules:**
- Maximum of 200 products allowed per wishlist
- Unique constraint on customer_id + product_id prevents duplicate entries
- Products must exist and not be soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
- Seller of the product must not be suspended

**Related Endpoints:**
- PATCH /customers/me/wishlist - View the paginated wishlist
- DELETE /customers/me/wishlist/{productId} - Remove a product from wishlist
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a wishlist entry linking the authenticated customer to a product.

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Extract customer ID from JWT authentication context
2. Validate productId exists in shopping_mall_products table
3. Verify product is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null)
4. Verify product's seller is not suspended
5. Check current wishlist count does not exceed 200 products for this customer
6. Use upsert pattern: if product already in wishlist, return existing entry; otherwise create new entry
7. Return created/existing wishlist entry with product summary information

**Database Operations:**
- SELECT from shopping_mall_products WHERE id = productId AND deleted_at IS NULL
- JOIN with shopping_mall_sellers to check seller status
- SELECT COUNT from shopping_mall_wishlists WHERE customer_id = authenticatedCustomerId
- INSERT into shopping_mall_wishlists (or return existing if duplicate)

**Error Handling:**
- 404: Product not found or deleted
- 400: Wishlist limit reached (200 products)
- 400: Product seller suspended
- 401: Authentication required

responseBody.description: Created wishlist entry with product summary information

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific wishlist entry by its unique identifier.

This operation allows an authenticated customer to view the details of a specific product they have saved to their wishlist. The response includes the wishlist entry metadata (when it was added, last updated) along with comprehensive product information.

**Security and Authorization:**
Only the customer who owns the wishlist entry can access this resource. If an authenticated customer attempts to access a wishlist entry belonging to another customer, the system returns a 403 Forbidden error. The ownership is verified by matching the authenticated customer's ID with the wishlist entry's customer_id field.

**Related Data:**
The wishlist entry references the shopping_mall_products table via product_id. The response includes product details such as the main image thumbnail, product name, base price or price range, seller shop name, and current availability status. If the product has been deleted by the seller, the entry will still exist but the product reference may be null.

**Use Case:**
This endpoint is useful when a customer wants to view detailed information about a specific saved product, or when the application needs to check the status of a wishlist entry (e.g., to display notifications about price changes or stock availability).
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the shopping_mall_wishlists table by primary key id to retrieve the wishlist entry. Join with shopping_mall_products to include product details (name, base_price, deleted_at). Join with shopping_mall_sellers to include seller shop information (shop_name). Join with shopping_mall_product_variants to calculate availability status and price range. Verify the authenticated customer's ID matches the wishlist entry's customer_id; if not, raise a 403 Forbidden error. If the wishlist entry does not exist, return a 404 Not Found error. Calculate the availability status: 'available' if at least one variant has stock > 0, 'out_of_stock' if all variants have stock = 0, 'unavailable' if product has no variants or is deleted. Return the complete wishlist entry with computed product summary information.

responseBody.description: The wishlist entry with product details

operations.description:
Removes a product from the authenticated customer's wishlist.

This operation permanently deletes a wishlist entry identified by its unique ID. The system verifies that the wishlist entry belongs to the currently authenticated customer before allowing deletion. This prevents customers from deleting wishlist entries belonging to other users.

When a wishlist entry is deleted:
- The entry is permanently removed from the database
- The product remains in the database and can be re-added to the wishlist later
- No snapshot is created (wishlist removal is not a financial transaction)

This operation does not affect:
- The product itself
- Any orders or reviews related to the product
- Other customers' wishlists containing the same product

Related operations:
- GET /wishlists - View all wishlist entries
- POST /wishlists - Add a product to wishlist
- PATCH /wishlists - Search/filter wishlist entries
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. **Authentication Verification**: Extract customer ID from JWT token in Authorization header. Return 401 Unauthorized if not authenticated.

2. **Input Validation**: Validate wishlistId is a valid UUID format. Return 400 Bad Request if invalid.

3. **Ownership Verification**: Query shopping_mall_wishlists table by id. If not found, return 404 Not Found. If found but customer_id does not match authenticated customer ID, return 403 Forbidden.

4. **Deletion**: Delete the wishlist entry from shopping_mall_wishlists table using the primary key.

5. **Response**: Return the deleted wishlist entry data for confirmation.

**Database Query**:
```sql
DELETE FROM shopping_mall_wishlists WHERE id = $1 AND customer_id = $2 RETURNING *
```

**Error Handling**:
- 401: Not authenticated
- 403: Wishlist entry belongs to different customer
- 404: Wishlist entry not found
- 400: Invalid wishlistId format

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of items in the customer's shopping cart.

This operation provides the authenticated customer with a comprehensive view of their cart contents, including product variant information, pricing, stock availability, and warnings for unavailable items.

Each cart item includes the product name, variant options (color, size, etc.), price per unit, quantity, and calculated subtotal. The response also indicates availability status - items are marked as unavailable if the product variant has been deleted or has insufficient stock.

The endpoint supports advanced filtering capabilities including availability status filtering and sorting by creation date or price. This enables customers to quickly identify problematic items before checkout.

Stock warnings are displayed for items with insufficient quantity, helping customers adjust their orders accordingly. Unavailable items (deleted variants or out-of-stock) are highlighted but preserved in the cart for customer visibility, allowing them to remove or modify items before proceeding to checkout.

This endpoint is typically used before checkout preparation to review cart contents and address any availability issues.
operations.name: index
